source.anchor_kjv: The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the city, and saith to the men, Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?
source.thread: A Samaritan woman came to a well for water; Jesus, a Jew, asked her for a drink and offered living water, a gift from God, a spring that never runs dry; He told her the truth of her life, knew it all, and stayed; He said He is the Christ; she left her jar and told the town; many called Him the Saviour of the world; He died for our sins and rose the third day

Jesus, a Jew, sits there, tired. JESUS: Give me to drink. WOMAN: How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me? NARRATOR: Jews and Samaritans kept apart. He asks anyway. JESUS: Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again. NARRATOR: Then He offers her a different water, a gift from God. Drink it, and you "shall never thirst": life from God inside you, a spring that never runs dry. NARRATOR: Then He tells her the truth about her life: five husbands, and the man she has now is not her husband. He knew it all, and stayed. NARRATOR: She says the Christ, the one God promised, will come. JESUS: I that speak unto thee am he. NARRATOR: He is the Christ. NARRATOR: She leaves her jar and goes back to town. WOMAN: Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ? NARRATOR: Many come, hear Him, and call Him "the Saviour of the world." NARRATOR: The jar stayed. She came for water, and found the One who gives better water: Jesus, who knew her whole story and offered her life. NARRATOR: To give that life, He died for our sins and rose the third day.

platforms.description:
She came to a well for water. She went home without her jar. Why?

The woman at the well (John 4): at noon a Samaritan woman meets Jesus, a Jew, who asks her for a drink. He offers her a different water, a gift from God, and tells her the truth about her whole life. He knew it all, and stayed. Then He tells her who He is.

"The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the city, and saith to the men, Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?" (John 4:28-29, KJV)

Read the whole story: John 4:4-42. Who in your life needs to hear about a man who knows everything and still stays?

platforms.description:
She came to a well for water. She went home without her jar. Why?

The woman at the well (John 4:4-42): at noon a Samaritan woman comes to draw water and finds Jesus, a Jew, sitting there tired. Jews and Samaritans kept apart, but He asks her for a drink anyway. Then He offers her a different water, a gift from God: whoever drinks it "shall never thirst", a spring of life from God that never runs dry. He tells her the truth about her life, five husbands and a man who is not her husband. He knew it all, and stayed. When she speaks of the Christ, the one God promised, Jesus says, "I that speak unto thee am he."

"The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the city, and saith to the men, Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?" (John 4:28-29, KJV)

Many in her town came, heard Him, and called Him "the Saviour of the world." She came for water and found the One who gives better water. To give that life, He died for our sins and rose the third day.

Read it: John 4:4-42.

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE

- instagram: "Then she ran to tell the town" -- the KJV says she "went her way into the city" (John 4:28); "ran" is the film's picture, not the text. Fix: "Then she went back to tell the town:".
- facebook: "offered her a water from God that never runs dry" -- "a water" is awkward for ESL readers and blurs the gift. Fix: "offered her water from God, a spring that never runs dry".
- youtube_short title: "| Jesus at the Well" -- the searched phrase is "woman at the well" (real autocomplete shows it; "jesus at the well" has none). The title loses its search half. Fix (owner's call, title is owner-locked): "Why Did She Leave Her Jar? | Woman at the Well". If kept, the description line 1 must carry "woman at the well" -- it does ("The woman at the well (John 4)"), so not blocking.
- all platforms: "He knew it all, and stayed" -- honest as the film's own line (He kept talking with her, and John 4:40 says He abode there two days), but stand-alone it can read as an unstated claim. Acceptable; do not add more to it.
- youtube_short: closing question "a man who knows everything and still stays" -- fine, grace-anchored, no pressure. Keep.
- tiktok: no verse quoted; first line is the hook -- fine for TikTok. Keep.
- KJV check: the John 4:28-29 quote is verbatim on YouTube short/long and Facebook; the Instagram quote (from "Come, see a man") is verbatim John 4:29. "I that speak unto thee am he" (John 4:26) and "shall never thirst" (John 4:14) and "the Saviour of the world" (John 4:42) are verbatim. No KJV error found.
- No clickbait, no overclaim, no shame on the woman; the five husbands are stated plainly once (long-form only) and framed by "He knew it all, and stayed." Pass on tone.
